2026-11-07.q: Which statement best captures the main point of the passage?
opts: A Russian extremist group has admitted planting explosives on an Aer Lingus flight.
A week-long wave of hoax bomb threats has disrupted flights, schools and media across Europe, and some analysts link it to Russian 'hybrid warfare'.
French prosecutors have charged the Irish captain of flight EI402 with refusing to land.
Italian schools were closed for a week after explosive devices were found in several buildings.
2026-11-07.exp: The passage opens with 'a sustained campaign of hoax bomb threats has caused considerable disruption throughout Europe', describes the diverted flight and the '279 fraudulent warnings' to Italian schools, and ends with analysts who 'interpret the campaign as a component of Russian ‘hybrid warfare’'. No group admitted anything, nobody was charged, and 'no explosive devices have been located'.

2026-11-07.q: What can be inferred about Anna Kruglova's view of the claim that a Russian extremist group sent the Dublin threat?
opts: She believes the group is real but too small to carry out an attack.
She thinks the Irish government invented the attribution.
She suspects the real senders may have used the group's name to make people more frightened.
She is certain the emails came from inside Ireland.
2026-11-07.exp: She 'considers this attribution unlikely' and argues that 'the perpetrators may deliberately adopt the identity of extremist organisations in order to maximise public anxiety'. Nothing suggests she blames the Irish government or knows where the emails came from.

2026-11-07.q: Why does the writer mention that 'more than 50 European leaders are scheduled to convene in Dublin next week'?
opts: To explain why the minister finds the threats especially worrying.
To show that the summit has been cancelled because of the threats.
To suggest that the European leaders sent the hoax emails.
To prove that the threats against Irish media were real.
2026-11-07.exp: McEntee 'characterised the events as extremely concerning, particularly given that more than 50 European leaders are scheduled to convene in Dublin next week'. The summit detail explains the extra concern; the passage does not say it was cancelled or link the leaders to the threats.

2026-11-07-2.q: What is the passage mainly about?
opts: LauraLynn is closing its home-based services to concentrate on hospital care.
The HSE is taking over the management of every children's charity in Ireland.
Charitable donations to LauraLynn will no longer be accepted after 2027.
The State will fully fund LauraLynn, Ireland's only children's hospice, bringing it under the HSE as a 'section 38' organisation.
2026-11-07-2.exp: The minister announced that LauraLynn 'will in future be funded entirely by the State' and 'will be designated a ‘section 38’ organisation; accordingly, the HSE will provide formal funding'. Its services continue, only LauraLynn is mentioned, and donations 'would remain essential'.

2026-11-07-2.q: What can be inferred about how LauraLynn's clinical services were paid for before this decision?
opts: They relied, at least partly, on fundraising.
They were already fully paid for by the HSE.
They were paid for entirely by the families of patients.
They were funded by the European Union.
2026-11-07-2.exp: The minister said the measure would 'eliminate its dependence on fundraising for clinical services', which implies those services had depended on fundraising. If the HSE already paid in full, no change would be needed; families and the EU are not mentioned.

2026-11-07-2.q: How would you describe Kerry McLaverty's reaction as reported in the passage?
opts: Angry that the State has taken so long and doubtful the money will arrive.
Indifferent, since the change will make little difference to the hospice.
Welcoming, while still stressing that donations remain important.
Worried that staff will lose their jobs when they become public servants.
2026-11-07-2.exp: She called the decision 'the culmination of many years of effort' (a positive view), 'nevertheless, she emphasised that charitable donations would remain essential'. There is no sign of anger, indifference or job fears.

2026-11-07-3.q: Which statement best summarises the passage?
opts: The High Court has blocked Bawag's offer for PTSB after complaints from minority shareholders.
Bawag's €1.6 billion takeover of PTSB has ECB approval but still needs High Court approval, and some shareholders oppose it.
The Minister for Finance has sold all of the State's shares in PTSB to Axis Capital.
Axis Capital has made a higher offer for PTSB than Bawag.

The court has not ruled ('A judgement is anticipated next week'), and Axis has only asked for time 'to prepare an alternative bid'.

2026-11-07-3.q: What can be inferred about Axis Capital from the passage?
opts: It is the largest shareholder in PTSB.
It has already completed a rival bid worth more than €2.97 per share.
It advises the Minister for Finance on the sale.
It did not yet have a competing offer ready to present.
2026-11-07-3.exp: Axis 'requested an adjournment of up to six weeks in order to prepare an alternative bid', so its bid was not ready, and the minister's lawyers said it was 'far from capable of submitting a viable offer'. The minister is the principal shareholder, and Axis is opposing, not advising, the minister.

2026-11-07-3.q: Why does the writer mention that the minister holds 'a substantial 57.5 per cent stake'?
opts: To show that the State is the key shareholder whose position matters to the deal.
To explain why the ECB had to approve the takeover.
To argue that the minister should refuse Bawag's offer.
To show that Bawag already owns most of PTSB.
2026-11-07-3.exp: The passage says 'the Minister for Finance remains the principal shareholder, with a substantial 57.5 per cent stake', which explains why the minister is a central party in the court case. It does not link the stake to the ECB's role, take sides, or say Bawag owns most of PTSB.

opts: The EU summits in Dublin have been moved because of protests by business owners.
Gardaí have ordered all businesses in the docklands to close for the summits.

Firms 'have not been instructed to close', and the summits are going ahead.

2026-11-07-4.q: What can be inferred about John O'Neill's business next week?
opts: It will earn more than usual because of summit visitors.
It will lose some income because customers who booked cruises must be refunded.
It will be closed for the whole week by Garda order.
It will move its cruises to another river.

2026-11-07-4.q: Which best describes John O'Neill's attitude to the security measures?
opts: Mixed: critical of how broad they are, but accepting that the events benefit the country.
Enthusiastic and fully supportive.
Completely uninterested.
Hostile, demanding that the summits be cancelled.
